notes.text: Available in cPanel 82 and later. Retrieves the selected account's archival settings. archive_logs, prune_archive and using_default are integer 0/1 flags in the pinned schema. retention_days is a number of days; zero retains logs indefinitely. When no custom retention value is set, retention_days is the server-wide default. using_default distinguishes default from custom retention.

The original 2026-10-31 capture on cPanel 11.138.0.19 observed numeric-string archive_logs, prune_archive and retention_days through direct UAPI and the WHM bridge. Structural types identify neither the quoted flag value nor whether both values occurred. Reviewer 5721279104 separately read explicit false/zero flags back after writes on that version.

Only archive_logs/prune_archive accept exact quoted 0/1 flags, and only retention_days accepts canonical signed decimal strings within PHP integer bounds, normalizing to integer results. Preserve omitted fields. using_default and sibling operation fields remain strict. Shared group requirements apply.

notes.text: Available in cPanel 82 and later. Saves the selected account's log archival settings. The pinned text requires at least one of archive_logs, prune_archive or retention_days.

archive_logs controls archiving to the home directory after statistics processing. Omission uses archive-logs in ~/.cpanel-logs, or default_archive-logs in cpanel.config when that file is absent. prune_archive controls removing the previous month's archives from ~/logs at month end. Omission uses remove-old-archived-logs in ~/.cpanel-logs, or default_remove-old-archive-logs in cpanel.config when that file is absent.

retention_days is in days: zero retains logs indefinitely; -1 clears the per-user override and restores the server default; positive integers retain logs for that many days. Omission preserves the existing value. The pinned schema declares a minimum of -1 but no maximum. Pruning and retention can remove archives. The pinned data schema is unconstrained.

Reviewer 5721279104 on cPanel 11.138.0.19 observed the server bound -1..999; 1000 raises ApiErrorException. Explicit false/zero flags were stored and read back. Omitted flags kept their current values with ~/.cpanel-logs present, including after retentionDays: -1. A call without arguments was server-rejected. These observations do not establish actual rotation or pruning.

Uses form POST. Null arguments are omitted; explicit false sends 0 and explicit zero is transmitted. Native optional bool/int inputs and server-side cross-field/range validation remain unchanged; no local minimum, maximum or enum check is added. Preserve every present JSON value and reject missing data. Shared group requirements apply.
Each call sends one request with no retry or undo. API success does not establish subsequent log rotation, pruning or retention enforcement.

notes.text: Available in cPanel 138 and later. Requires a domain owned by the selected account and the exact file_id selector: php_fpm_error_log (home logs directory), docroot_error_log (domain document root), or homedir_error_log (home directory).

Reads trailing PHP error-log lines in chronological order, oldest first. Omitted limit uses the server default of 100; the documented minimum is 1 and values above 5000 are silently capped by the server.

log_content is a string list, empty for an empty log. lines_read is the returned integer line count in the pinned schema; partial=1 means the file exceeds limit. modified_today uses the server date/time. mtime and size are integer Unix time and bytes. Flags are integer 0/1; fields are optional.

Reviewer 5721279104 on cPanel 11.138.0.19 observed lines_read as the digit string "0" for an empty log through direct UAPI, with log_content: []. Nonempty direct and bridged reads returned native integer counts. Neither committed log-administration capture contains view_error_log.

Only lines_read additionally accepts canonical signed decimal strings within PHP integer bounds and normalizes them to int; native integers and omission remain intact. No range or nonnegative check is added. Sibling mtime, size and flags remain strict. The supplied limit is sent unchanged. Private log_content and explicitly accessible PayloadMismatchException payloads must not be logged; they stay out of exception messages and trace arguments. Shared group requirements and filesystem policy apply.
Each call sends one request with no retry or undo. API success does not establish subsequent log rotation, pruning or retention enforcement.
